- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day for remaining horizon.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast for 1–3 days ahead to catch momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model in last 5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is high and model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3 days.
